title: SYSK Selects: Was Atlantis A Real Place?
summary: A SYSK Selects rerun, chosen by Josh, examining whether Atlantis was a real place. The hosts trace Atlantis to Plato's dialogues (Timaeus and Critias, c. 360 BC), the later pseudo-historical claims of Ignatius Donnelly (1882) and Edgar Cayce, and the wide range of places Atlantis has been placed. They then turn to Helike, a wealthy ancient Greek city on the Gulf of Corinth, destroyed by an earthquake and tsunami in 373 BC and later buried by river silt. Archaeologists have uncovered Helike's ruins beneath later Roman, Byzantine and Bronze Age layers, and the hosts argue it may have inspired Plato's story. A listener mail segment promotes the Celebrity Bookends fundraiser for Cooperative for Education (Co-Ed) in Guatemala.

segments.title: Selects intro and opening banter
segments.summary: Josh introduces the episode as his selected pick, and the hosts banter about being back in the studio after time in Texas. Chuck asks whether Atlantis is real.

segments.title: Plato's Atlantis and the Donnelly-era myths
segments.summary: The hosts note Plato is the only ancient source for Atlantis, written in about 360 BC in the Timaeus dialogue, and suggest it was an allegory. They say Plato placed it past the Pillars of Hercules and nine thousand years earlier. They credit Ignatius Donnelly's 1882 book with launching fringe theories, and list places Atlantis has been placed, including Edgar Cayce's claims about the Bermuda Triangle.

segments.title: Introducing Helike
segments.summary: Josh reveals Helike, a powerful ancient Greek city on the Gulf of Corinth. It had colonies, led the Achaean League, minted coins with Poseidon, and had a famous statue of Poseidon, drawing parallels to Atlantis.

segments.title: Destruction of Helike in 373 BC
segments.summary: In 373 BC animals fled to the hills, then an earthquake and a huge wave struck in the night and submerged the city. Survivors could not be found, and ten Spartan ships in the port vanished. The submerged city, including the Poseidon statue, remained visible for centuries and was described by travelers.

segments.title: Why Helike was buried: fault lines, rivers and silt
segments.summary: The hosts explain that Helike sat between fault lines and where three rivers met, which made it fertile but seismically dangerous. Silt from the rivers and a rising delta buried the city over time. They also discuss rising sea levels and underwater settlements such as Doggerland.

segments.title: Archaeological discovery of Helike
segments.summary: Cornell researchers searched for Helike in the late 1980s, and a Greek colleague's translation suggested it was inland in a lagoon rather than in the gulf. A German archaeologist's Poseidon coin and a Roman ruin about twelve feet down led to finds including Roman, Byzantine and Bronze Age layers, a Roman road, skeletons, jugs, a sea wall and the possible Spartan ships. Excavation has continued, with digging starting in earnest around 2000.

segments.title: Celebrity Bookends fundraiser
segments.summary: A listener describes the Celebrity Bookends campaign to raise money for Cooperative for Education in Guatemala by making bookends famous through social media and selling them for a million dollars. The hosts give Facebook, Twitter and email contacts.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Hosts sign off and point listeners to the website for more on Helike and the show's contact channels.
